requirement: The `habeas` skill MUST tell agents that a new project with little code starts with `habeas-requirements`, not `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`, even though most of its code has no references.
rationale:
structural: The text of `requirements.cli.overview_skill.new_project` says only that the `habeas` skill MUST tell agents that a new project with little code starts with `habeas-requirements`, not `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`, even though most of its code has no references. That is a content obligation, and it specifies no library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or delegation through a named interface. An alternative that put the same guidance in a different section or wording would still satisfy the text. So there is no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence.

The root `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` does contain the guidance. A search found it in `section[Habeas]/section[Workflow]`: "A new project with little code starts with habeas-requirements, not habeas-bootstrap-requirements, even though most of its code has no references."

behavioral: The requirement has one observable obligation. The `habeas` skill MUST tell agents that a new project with little code starts with `habeas-requirements`, not `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`, even though most of its code has no references.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_habeas_skill_starts_a_new_project_with_the_requirements_skill]` is marked {test} for this requirement. It reads step 1 of the `habeas` skill's workflow with `step("habeas", 1)`. It uses `assert_text`, which asserts that the text contains each phrase and fails otherwise. It checks two phrases:

- The routing row "Adopting Habeas in an existing codebase, or most of the code has no references | habeas-bootstrap-requirements". This confirms that the bootstrap skill is reserved for the existing-codebase case.
- The sentence "A new project with little code starts with habeas-requirements, not habeas-bootstrap-requirements, even though most of its code has no references". This covers every element of the obligation: the new-project case, the `habeas-requirements` skill, the exclusion of `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`, and the unreferenced-code caveat.

The helpers `step` and `workflow_steps` read the skill's Workflow section, and `step` panics if the step is missing. The test therefore fails if the skill text is removed or changed. No other input classes or boundaries are named. Because the obligation concerns skill text, a content assertion is the appropriate check.
